sentences.text: The petitioners in O.P.(M.V.) No.1875/2007 on the file of the IInd Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Kollam, are the appellants herein.

entities.text: IInd Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Kollam
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: (For the purpose of convenience, the parties are hereafter referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal)

2. The O.P. was filed under under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, by the wife, child and mother of the deceased by name Sukesan, who died in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 12.02.2007.
According to them, on 12.02.2007, at about 03.45 pm, while the deceased was riding a motorcycle, he was knocked down by a car driven by the 1 st respondent in a rash and negligent manner.
As a result of which, he sustained serious injuries and he succumbed to the injuries on the very same day.
3. The 1st respondent is the driver cum owner and the 2nd respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
According to the petitioners, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.

The quantum of compensation claimed in the O.P. was Rs.6,00,000/-.
4.
The insurance company filed a written statement, admitting the accident as well as policy, but disputing the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.

The evidence in the case consists of the documentary evidence Exts.A1 to A7.
6.

After evaluating the evidence on record, the Tribunal found negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, awarded a total compensation of Rs.5,03,500/- and directed the insurer to pay the same.
7. Aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the petitioners preferred this appeal.

8. Now the point that arises for consideration is the following:
Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable?
Shyamala vs New India Assurance Co.Ltd on 11 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191634369/
2 9.

sentences.text: Heard Sri.K.Siju, the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioners/appellants, and Sri.Mathews Jacob, the learned Senior Standing Counsel for the 2nd respondent as instructed by Sri.P.Jacob Mathew.
10. The Point: In this case the accident as well as valid policy of the offending vehicle are admitted.
One of the contentions raised by the learned counsel for the petitioners is regarding the income of the deceased as fixed by the Tribunal.
As per the claim petition, the deceased was working as a driver by profession earning Rs.6,000/- per month, but the Tribunal fixed his monthly income at Rs.4,000/-.The learned counsel for the insurer
would argue that the income fixed by the tribunal is reasonable.

As per the dictum laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236], the notional income of a coolie, during the year 2007 will come to Rs.6,000/-.

entities.text: Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the decision in Kantha Swamy and others v. E John and others (MACA No.3326 of 2017 dated 19.03.2025), this Court has fixed the notional income of a driver involved in an accident in the year 2007 at Rs.8,000/-.

entities.text: Kantha Swamy and others v. E John and others (MACA No.3326 of 2017
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioners have produced Ext.A7 driving licence of the deceased to prove that he was a driver by profession.
Therefore, his notional income is fixed at Rs.8,000/-, for the purpose of computing the loss of dependency.
12. On the date of accident, the deceased was aged 42 years.

Therefore, 25% of the monthly income is liable to be added towards future prospects, as held in the decision in National Insurance Co.Ltd v Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680] and the multiplier to be applied is 14, as held in Sarla Verma v.
Delhi Transport Corporation, (2009) 6 SCC 121.

entities.text: National Insurance Co.Ltd v Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text:
Sarla Verma v.
Delhi Transport Corporation, (2009) 6 SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Since the deceased was married who left behind 3 dependents, towards personal and living expense, 1/3 of the income is liable to be deducted, as held in Sarla Verma (supra).
In the above circumstances, the loss of dependency will come to Rs.11,20,000/-.

13. The Tribunal has awarded Rs.5,000/- towards loss of estate, MACA NO. 1535 OF 2014 2025:KER:32469 Rs.5,000/- towards funeral expenses, Rs.15,000/- towards loss of consortium and Rs.25,000/- towards love and affection.

In the light of the decision in Pranay Sethi (supra), the appellants are entitled to get a consolidated sum of Rs.15,000/- towards loss of estate, Rs.15,000/-
towards funeral expenses, and the dependents (parents, children and spouse) are entitled to get a sum of Rs.40,000/- each towards loss of consortium, with an increase of 10% in every three years.

Therefore, towards loss of estate and funeral expense they are entitled to get a sum of Rs.18,150/-
each.

Towards loss of consortium, petitioners together are entitled to get a sum of Rs.1,45,200/-
(48,400 x 3).
14.

Since compensation for loss of consortium was given, further compensation for love and affection cannot be granted, in view of the decision in New India Assurance Company Ltd. v.
Somwati and Others, [(2020)9 SCC 644].

sentences.text: Towards the head 'pain and sufferings', the Tribunal has not granted any compensation.
The deceased died in this case on the date of the accident.

In the above circumstances, I am inclined to grant Rs.25,000/- towards pain and suffering.
16.
No change is required, in the amounts awarded on other heads, as the compensation awarded on those heads appears to be just and reasonable.

Therefore, the petitioners/appellants are entitled to get a total compensation of Rs.13,32,000/-,
as modified and recalculated above and given in the table below, for easy reference:

Sl.
 No. Head of Claim Amount awarded by Amount Awarded in  Tribunal (in Rs.) Appeal (in Rs.)
 1 Transportation expenses 5000 5000  3 Funeral expenses 5000 18,150  4 Loss of dependency 448000 11,20,000  5 Loss of consortium 15,000 1,45,200  6 Loss of love and affection 25,000 Nil
7 Loss of estate 5,000 18,150
8 Pain and sufferings Nil 25,000  Total 5,03,500 13,32,000  Enhanced to Rs. 8,28,500 18.

In the result, this Appeal is allowed in part, and the 2nd respondent is directed to deposit a total sum of Rs.13,32,000/- (Rupees Thirteen Lakhs Thirty Two Thousand Only), less the amount already deposited, if any, along with interest @ 8% per annum from the date of the petition till MACA NO. 1535 OF 2014 2025:KER:32469 realisation/deposit, excluding interest for a period of 597 days, the period of delay in filing the appeal, with proportionate costs, within a period of two months from today.

On depositing the aforesaid amount, the Tribunal shall disburse the entire amount to the petitioners, in the ratio fixed by the Tribunal, excluding court fee payable, if any, without delay, as Shyamala vs New India Assurance Co.Ltd on 11 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191634369/
4 per rules.
